scope: Ordinary hosted production-seed input. Version 3 preserves all 267 version-2 source fixtures, diagnostics and successful program expectations, explicitly migrating rejection to stderr, empty stdout and status 1. Leading emit routes are excluded. Lexical, structural then native diagnostic priority remains unchanged; this is not globally earliest-error selection or complete language verification. Additional independently expected control-flow combinations cover nested returns, live continuation types, branch-local initialization, and nested short-circuit evaluation order and stack joins. Never-returning helper cases pin that a helper counts as never returning only when a fresh empty array is bound before each return that reads it, and that main is never such a helper. Statement calls (2026-10-20) changed nine expectations that had pinned `do` of a value call as ERR 404: each now expects the result of the same call bound by `let` to an unused name, as do the statement-call cases. Separate CLI contract tests output publication and injected I/O faults. Loop cases (2026-10-21, `while-*`) take their run expectations from a hand-written recursive twin of each program compiled by the seed before loops existed, and their rejections from the if-shaped behaviour of that seed. The 2026-10-27 cases pin what the mutant run found unpinned: bitwise complement, shift and `and` values, buffer_get and buffer_set bounds and byte range, buffer_copy source spans and linux_syscall6 argument order, plus ERR 420/430/429 reject coverage for buffer_get, buffer_set, buffer_length, buffer_address and linux_syscall6, one case each, the codes buffer_copy and buffer_fill already have. Two more cases the same day pin what that batch's review found still unpinned: an upward overlapping buffer_copy of twelve bytes, which runs the eight-byte backward step once and the byte tail four times, and a buffer_copy destination start past the destination's length. The 2026-10-27 diagnostics cases pin the nesting limit from both sides (a flat sum of 2,000 terms and 1,999 nested ifs compile; 2,001 terms and 2,000 ifs are refused with ERR 405 at the first node past the limit), the array-of-unknown ERR 438 program the K1 review wrote, and a located ERR 430 and ERR 433 on a never-returning helper's result; the same day the missing-return cases moved from ERR 424/415/416 to ERR 406 at the function's own line and the ERR 436 case gained its line. The K3 cases (2026-10-27) pin the \t, \r and \0 escapes in strings and chars and how main renders them, a backslash-space still unnamed, and the four ERR 429 function-table texts; the same day the nine reserved-name cases took the ERR 429 text that names the builtin and the two unknown-escape cases the ERR 104 text that names the escape. The K4 cases (2026-10-28) pin the located division-by-zero message for / and % on different lines (a modulo inside a helper, and a modulo by zero in a tuple after good divisions), output written before the fault kept, and the out-of-memory message when one buffer_fill asks for more than the 3.5 GiB heap, which fails before any memory is touched. The set cases (2026-10-31) pin `do set(a, i, v)`: in-place replacement of the first, last and a middle entry for ints, bools, strings, tuples, value and reference records, nested arrays, 18-word entries and 15-word entries (the one width whose position and array loads take different displacement sizes); an alias, a helper's parameter and a later add seeing the change; the located bounds fault in get's shape with `set:` at the count, far beyond, on an empty array, at a wrapped position and for 18- and 15-word entries, with output written before it kept and nothing after it; twenty million sets in a loop moving the heap by nothing; and ERR 420 (too few and too many arguments), 440, 429, 447, 435, 436 and 430 at their lines. The local-environment cases (2026-10-31, `locals-*`), written when the compiler began storing a new local in place over a dead one, pin that reuse: an if's three arms each declaring 60 or 40 locals of different types past positions 128 and 1,248 and the code after the join declaring as many again, a while body declaring 40 locals across a 32-entry boundary on every pass, and a local rebound in an arm before a let; every local is read, and the expected sums are computed outside the compiler.
